name: Wi-Fi Strength
notes:
Port of `wifi_strength`: a centred line whose LENGTH runs 0.1-1.0 and whose COLOUR runs red to green, both off one number, `t = clamp((rssi + 90) / 40)`.

One number driving a whole shape's colour is `paletteSpan` 0. With the span at zero the index collapses and `t = paletteOffset`, so every pixel of the line takes the same colour and a row on the offset picks it off the two-entry ramp. `wrap` is off, so the palette is a gradient with two ends rather than a ring -- red at 0, green at 1.

THE ANIMATION HAS NO USER PARAMETERS. Its only entry is `Parameter::Internal("rssi")`, and nothing in a patch can reach RSSI, heap or link state (LIFE-683), so the rack is one knob standing in for the reading. Note that CLAUDE.md's animation table lists `color_poor`, `color_good` and `color_excellent` for this animation; `wifi_strength.cpp` declares none of them and hardcodes red-to-green. The code is what this ports.

The animation eases toward the true RSSI at 3/s. A macro is human input and is smoothed upstream at about 5 Hz, which is close enough that nothing was built for it.
